cohort: The study included 4858 infants 22-26 weeks of gestation born 2006-2011 at 24 US hospitals participating in the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Neonatal Research Network.
finding: Infants born at 23 weeks were more frequently resuscitated without antenatal corticosteroids, and consistently providing antenatal corticosteroids for resuscitated 23-week infants was projected to increase infant survival and survival without impairment.
